prerequisites: Basic knowledge of IT and a programming language

learning_outcomes.text: Students can analyze data management tasks with adequate methods and find solutions based on structured approaches. They can understand and use processes in existing data management systems. They know starting points for improvements using professional tools and technologies, and can define and document them.

Students are able to find and understand specialized literature on data management in general and specifically on product lifecycle management methods. Based on the developed conceptual and technical foundations, students can classify innovative approaches.

Students master selected concepts and tools of professional information technology. They understand current and professional software systems for designing databases and managing product data and can use them effectively. They evaluate data management approaches and tools in relation to specific tasks and assess their suitability.

Students can analyze and critically evaluate existing and new data management concepts. Students are able to evaluate and actively participate in shaping the use of and critical engagement with information technology concepts in the professional world.

Students can identify the challenges in the conception and use of distributed information technology solutions. They can summarize technical, organizational, and ethical issues related to the use of data management systems. They can actively and soundly discuss these issues with stakeholders, even controversially.

syllabus_topics: Client/server technologies in the business environment
Data management systems, Product Lifecycle Management (PLM)
Product and process data in PDM systems. Resource utilization and sustainability aspects.
Exchange of product data, OEM-supplier scenarios
PLM concepts in the business IT environment, interfaces to ERP and other systems
ERP systems and their importance for product development and production
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is an oral examination. The ungraded assessment is a written project report of 4-8 pages, plus the concept and implementation of a database model. Specific duration and scope for the oral examination are governed by the currently valid General Examination Regulations.
